newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Bank Leumi 3Q EPS 0.121 shekel vs 0.056.
newsitem.headline: Bank Leumi 3Q EPS 0.121 shekel vs 0.056.

text.p: Bank Leumi, Israel's second-largest banking group, attributed improved earnings for the third quarter and nine months to expanding business operations, higher earnings at subsidiaries and a reduced provision for doubtful debt.

The bank took a one-time provision of 190.3 million shekels to cover the expenses of a voluntary retirement scheme for 312 employees. Without the provision, nine-month net earnings would have been 494.8 million shekels, Leumi said.

Based on its nine-month net earnings, Leumi showed a net annualised return on capital of 7.7 percent, compared with 7.4 percent in the year-earlier period. Discounting the cost of the retirement scheme, the return was 9.8 percent.
Leumi said shareholders' equity grew 5.8 percent from the end of 1995 to 7.183 billion shekels as of September 30.
Credit to the public increased 9.0 percent from a year earlier to 76.7 billion shekels as of September 30, while deposit froms the public rose 9.6 percent to 101.0 billion shekels.
Total assets amounted to 126.2 billion shekels, an increase of 3.5 percent from the end of 1995.

Leumi said the gains from the sales of partial stakes in Leumi Insurance Holdings Ltd and Africa Israel Investments Ltd would amount to about 400 million shekels. The gains will be registered in subsequent quarters.
